data.description: A 57-year-old female without any medical history was admitted for evaluation of a left ventricular tumor that was discovered incidentally. The patient was asymptomatic and had no relevant past medical history. Physical examination findings were not specifically described in the case report.

A rare benign vascular tumor of the heart composed of proliferating blood vessels. It can arise in the left ventricular myocardium and is often found incidentally; imaging may show marked or progressive contrast enhancement.
symptoms_in_common: Incidental discovery of a left ventricular mass
Imaging appearance of a vascular-appearing cardiac lesion

data.description: A histologic subtype of cardiac hemangioma characterized by dilated vascular spaces within fibrous tissue. These benign tumors may be intramyocardial and can be clinically silent.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent vascular spaces and fibrous stroma on pathology images

data.description: A rare benign malformation or tumor of lymphatic vessels that can occur in the myocardium or pericardium. It may appear as a cystic or vascular cardiac mass and is often asymptomatic.
symptoms_not_in_common: No cystic or pericardial predominance was described

data.description: A benign tumor composed predominantly of dense fibrous connective tissue, usually arising within ventricular myocardium. It is more common in children but can occasionally occur in adults.
symptoms_in_common: Fibrous tissue visible on pathology staining
symptoms_not_in_common: Patient is an adult, whereas cardiac fibroma more commonly occurs in children
Prominent vascular channels and enhancement are less typical for a fibroma

data.description: The most common primary benign cardiac tumor, usually arising in the left atrium from the interatrial septum. It may be asymptomatic or cause obstructive, embolic, or constitutional symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Female patient in the typical age range for myxoma
Cardiac mass may be found incidentally
symptoms_not_in_common: Mass is located in the left ventricle rather than the usual left atrial location
No constitutional symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or fatigue
Imaging and pathology appear more vascular and fibrous than typical myxoma
